title: Publish the null-spelling bounds in limits
lead: `fields[].nullSpellings` and `table.rowClasses.allNullRowSpellings` keep at most 64 distinct spellings of at most 256 characters each (`SpellingCounter.MaxSpellings`, `MaxLength`) and count the rest in `nullSpellingsOther` and `allNullRowSpellingsOther`. Both bounds are internal constants. Publish them in the descriptor's `limits` block and document them in docs/descriptor.md. **Not in this slice:** making the bounds configurable; changing their values; counting the distinct spellings in the "other" counters (the next item).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A downstream consumer that must know whether a spelling was dropped has to hard-code 64 and 256 and re-check them on every squalify version bump. sq-36 shipped them as fixed and unpublished, and descriptor.md says so ("these two bounds are fixed, they are not in `limits`"); a consumer that reads `limits` is the one place it already looks for caps (`nullTokens`, `unitTable`, `shapeCharsPerField`, `budget`, the sq-38 sketch levels).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `Limits` and `Limits.Default` (`src/squalify/Descriptor/Options.cs`), `SpellingCounter` and `FieldAccumulator` (`src/squalify/Fields/`, the constants), `DescriptorWriter` (`src/squalify/Json/DescriptorWriter.cs`)
- docs/descriptor.md (the `limits` section, the `nullSpellings` and `allNullRowSpellings` paragraphs that say the bounds are not in `limits`, the consumer subset and versioning policy), design.md, user-guide.md; every golden descriptor if the members are always written
- This record is also edited by sq-38 and sq-41; the later of them merges main first

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- **Published:** a profiled descriptor's `limits` carries the 64 and 256 under the chosen names, and they equal the constants the counter enforces (one source of truth: the test reads the counter's constants, so changing one without the other fails).
- **Enforced:** a field with 65 distinct null spellings keeps 64 and counts the 65th in `nullSpellingsOther`, and a spelling of 257 characters is counted there too, so the published bounds are the real ones (guards against the limits drifting from the behavior).
- **Documented:** a docs test, in the style of the existing descriptor.md tests, checks the two members are described, and the stale sentence "not in `limits`" is gone from descriptor.md and design.md.
- **Goldens:** every golden is rewritten once and the diff is only the new `limits` members (review the diff); fingerprints are unchanged (check whether `limits` enters any projection; it must not move a hash).
- **Schema/consumer subset (pending Q1, Q2):** the members are listed in the consumer-subset table with their stability class, as the existing limits members are.
- Mutation-check: changing one published value, and publishing the wrong constant, each fail a test above.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Build, test and format pass; `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: The owner commits. Do not commit; never add Co-Authored-By or similar lines.
